precepts.why: “But Rhodocus, who was in the Jews’ host, disclosed the secrets to the enemies; therefore he was sought out, and when they had gotten him, they put him in prison.” Rhodocus was one of our people who sold us out and gave information to the enemy. Some in the camp right now are Rhodocus, women and brothers, FBI, CIA: that is on you.

points: You don't find out what happened to Menelaus until chapter 13. Menelaus joined himself with them, and with great dissimulation encouraged Antiochus, not for the safeguard of the country, but because he thought to have been made ruler. If I can't be high priest again, I'll be governor.

But the King of kings moved Antiochus's mind against this wicked wretch: one day you are friends, and the Most High says, no, that is not your friend. Lysias informed the king that this man was the cause of all mischief, so the king commanded to bring him unto Berea and to put him to death: a tower of fifty cubits high, full of ashes, into which men thrust whosoever was condemned of sacrilege.

Such a death it happened that wicked man to die, not having so much as burial in the earth; and that most justly: for inasmuch as he had committed many sins about the altar, whose fire and ashes were holy, he received his death in ashes. He got his just reward.

If you are not a nationalist you cannot be a revolutionist: you cannot start a revolution if you do not love your nation or do not want a nation. When the Greeks tried to rule over us, Mattathias and his sons rose up and started a revolution. Judas determined “to go forth and try the matter in fight by the help of the Lord”: he was ready to shed blood, and in every revolution there is bloodshed.

He “exhorted his soldiers to fight manfully, even unto death, for the laws, the temple, the city, the country”. All revolutionaries understand they can die in what they do. Judas Maccabeus and his men were not only revolutionaries but nationalists: they loved their nation and their people. A revolutionary is a nationalist ready to die for his country and his people.
